text:
Ethan: Heads-up thread: I prototyped a 'predictive escrow' idea for smoothing sudden credit bursts across heterogeneous model pools. Wanted quick feedback on contract + failure modes before I put it in an RFC.

Priya: Short summary?

Ethan: Idea: instead of strict immediate quota checks, edges can request a small temporary escrow of cost-credits for upcoming work. Escrow has short TTL and conservative caps. Scheduler later reconciles actual usage and issues ADJUSTs via ledger.

Camille: So edges would optimistically admit using escrow tokens and avoid a sync call to central for each request?

Ethan: Exactly. Common path: edge gets local lease + occasional escrow grant for bursts (e.g., sudden fanout from client). Saves p95.

Diego: Main risk is overspend if many edges get escrows and then all use them. How do we prevent global credit violation?

Ethan: Two controls: 1) escrow minted only when central scheduler has headroom based on recent consumption curves; 2) per-client escrow cap = min(global_headroom * alpha, client_budget * beta). We tune alpha/beta.

Priya: Need formula and invariants. We must ensure: sum(allocated_escrow) + committed_balance <= total_budget + epsilon. Epsilon is small and bounded.

Camille: Also need quick revocation path: central should be able to revoke outstanding escrows via push (pub/sub) and edges must stop admitting when revoked.

Ethan: Agreed. Revocations published to a short-topic; edges subscribe and immediately invalidate any matching escrow keys. We'll include escrow_version in admits.

Diego: What about split-brain/regional headroom differences? A region might think it has headroom while global is constrained.

Ethan: We'll scope escrows by region and have a global safety budget that central uses to limit per-region allocation. Allocation logic: per_region_headroom = min(region_capacity, global_remaining*region_weight).

Priya: Good. Telemetry: escrow_granted, escrow_used, escrow_revoked, escrow_stale_apply, reconciliation_adjust. Need to track who used escrow vs who used actual lease.

Camille: Failure modes: central down -> no new escrows, edges fallback to local conservative token-bucket. But what about already-granted escrows while central is down?

Ethan: Escrows are TTL-limited (e.g., 5s). If central is down longer than TTL, escrows expire naturally. If central is down but edge still has unconsumed escrows, they can be used but we mark them as 'untrusted' and log for reconciliation. Prefer conservative default: do not allow use beyond a safe fraction when control plane unreachable.

Diego: How to reconcile billing when predicted cost != actual (models cheaper/more expensive due to batching)?

Ethan: Ledger ADJUSTs apply post-hoc. If actual cost > escrowed cost, central emits negative ADJUSTs to charge back. If less, central credits back. We cap post-hoc debits to avoid surprising customers: policies can set max_recovery_pct.

Priya: For fairness, need to decide whether escrow counts against fairness immediately or only after reconciliation. Otherwise a tenant could use many escrows and force others to be shed.

Camille: I think escrow should temporarily decrement a 'soft_balance' used for local admits. Scheduler runs frequent rebalances that convert soft_balance -> hard_balance. Hard_balance enforces global fairness.

Ethan: Exactly: soft_balance is speculative; hard_balance is authoritative. When rebalancer sees imbalance, it writes ADJUSTs to drain soft balances from aggressive clients.

Diego: Implementation: escrow records = {client_id, escrow_id, tokens_cost, expires_at, version, region}. Keep schema tiny. Use compacted topic for live state and non-compacted for events.

Priya: Security/Private deploys: escrows are optional. Customers can disable or set alpha=0. Also must avoid sending raw model names; use model_hash or local mapping.

Camille: Ops alerting: ledger_reconcile_latency, escrow_revocation_latency, sum_escrow_outstanding_pct. ops-bot should page if outstand_pct > 1% of total budget for >2m.

ops-bot: :warning: Suggested alert - escrow_outstanding_pct_3m > 1% -> Pager to oncall. Playbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/escrow-oversubscribe

Ethan: Rollout plan: 1) shadow mode where we issue escrows but don't allow edges to use them; 2) canary: enable usage for small % of traffic with strict caps; 3) increase regionally while monitoring reconciliation noise and ADJUST rates.

Priya: Metrics to watch during canary: reconciliation_adjust_rate, customer_dispute_count, p95_admit_latency, ledger_lag, and cost_recovery_rate.

Diego: Edge changes: small cache for escrow grants keyed by escrow_id and policy_version. Admit path must fast-check local unconsumed escrow_count before consulting leases.

Camille: What about per-request logging overhead? Keep sampling and only full logs for errors/adapt events.

Ethan: Agreed. Also include a lightweight feature_hash in admits for de-dup and sampling.

Priya: One more: what happens during model migrations where cost_model changes? Escrow used under old cost assumptions could be underpriced. Need aggressive ADJUST caps and maybe temporary escrow_pause during big costshock events.

Ethan: We can publish cost_model_version. If we detect a cost_model bump > threshold, we flip to conservative mode: no escrow grants and ramp policies.

Diego: I can prototype edge client changes if we agree on small escrow API now.

Ethan: API sketch:
```
POST /v1/escrow/grant
{ client_id, region, requested_cost_hint }
=> {escrow_id, cost_granted, expires_at, escrow_version}

POST /v1/escrow/revoke
{ escrow_id }
=> { revoked: true }
```
Edges include escrow_id header when admitting.

Priya: Okay. This is promising. Please put a concise summary + failure-mode table into an RFC PR. Mention configuration knobs for Private deployments.

Ethan: Will do. Target RFC by EOD Friday. Thanks all :rocket:
